answer: The Biomedical Engineering program prepares students for careers in biomedical/clinical engineering, solving complex healthcare problems with modern tools, teamwork and communication, lifelong learning and graduate study; objectives include excellence, leadership-oriented education, solving societal problems and multidisciplinary research.

answer: Biomedical Engineering adopts the seven ABET student outcomes: solving complex engineering problems, engineering design, communication, ethical and professional responsibility, teamwork, experimentation and data analysis, and acquiring new knowledge.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering program in Biomedical Engineering is accredited by the
answer: The Bachelor of Engineering in Biomedical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria and Program Criteria for Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

source_quote: perform well in advanced therapeutic and surgical devices, medical imaging, artificial
answer: Biomedical engineers develop tools and machines to improve health and diagnosis, working with healthcare professionals on therapeutic and surgical devices, medical imaging, artificial organs, physiological modeling, rehabilitation, biorobotics and medical equipment management; the field is described as fast-growing.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering (BE) degree in the BIOM Engineering program comprises
answer: The BE in Biomedical Engineering is 152 credits over eight regular and three summer semesters; the BS is 118 credits over six regular and three summer semesters. Both require a CGPA, major GPA and SLP grade of 70 or above.
BS in Biomedical Engineering (118 credits): General Education 27 (23%), College Requirements 24 (20%), Program Requirements 67 (57%); major 46 mandatory, non-major 65 mandatory + 7 elective.

BE in Biomedical Engineering (152 credits): General Education 30 (20%), College Requirements 27 (18%), Program Requirements 95 (62%: 80 mandatory + 15 technical elective); major 56 mandatory + 15 elective, non-major 71 mandatory + 10 elective.

Biomedical mandatory courses: BIOM 301/301L, 311, 312/312L, 313, 400 (BS project; BE takes electives instead), 414, 415L, 417, 418, 421, 440, 499 Co-op, 519, 522, 531, 595A, 595B; CCEE 221/221L, 331, 426/426L, 460/460L, 534; ELEC 200, 320/320L, 340, Power Electronics, and ELEC 451.

answer: The Biomedical SLP is 3 credits for the BS and 4 credits for the BE, done preferably in groups on an industry or community problem; the text says 3 credits in the first regular semester and 1 credit in the next.
review_note: Split order conflicts with BIOM 595A (1 credit) and BIOM 595B (3 credits) and with other engineering programs (1 then 3).

source_quote: Students must complete 8 weeks of practical training working in an area related to their
answer: Biomedical students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (BIOM 499, 3 credits), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, a formal report, poster and presentation; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.
